cells.quote: The studies yielded inconclusive results, had important methodological flaws, and reported insufficient or no information about important aspects of the materials, procedure and key requirements from students and instructors to guarantee the success of PjBL.
cells.note: The review reports mixed findings across eleven controlled studies: seven reported positive results, two reported no significant differences, one reported no quantitative data, and one offered no comparison. No quantitative meta-analysis was performed.

cells.quote: The articles aimed at examining the impact of PjBL in kindergarten and primary students were scarce and, overall, yielded mixed results. Specifically, seven of the 11 studies included in this review obtained positive results regarding the impact of PjBL in academic achievement of students immediately after the intervention [36,38,41,42,46,47] or in the long term [44]. Among the rest, two studies did not find significant differences between the experimental and control groups [37,43], one study did not report any quantitative data [40], and another one offered no comparison between the experimental and control groups [39].
cells.note: This was a systematic review without a quantitative meta-analysis; the included studies varied in participants, intervention duration, and measured outcomes.

O.outcome_detail: perceived relevance and alignment with clinical practice

cells.quote: In all four student focus groups, participants emphasized the overall relevance of the examination and its close alignment with clinical practice.
cells.note: The study reports a qualitative perception, not a comparison with another examination format or condition.

cells.quote: However, time constraints during the OSCE and the associated stress were consistently identified as negative aspects.
cells.note: The study reports negative qualitative perceptions, but provides no comparison condition; therefore direction relative to a comparator is not coded.

cells.quote: On a 15-point grading scale, students rated the PJ-OSCE with a mean score of 10.90/15 points (SD 2.54; n = 225).
cells.note: Descriptive post-examination rating; the study reports no comparison condition.

cells.quote: 41% of students reported a large or very large subjective learning gain.
cells.note: Descriptive self-report after the examination; the study reports no comparison condition.

cells.quote: The reduced time of 8 min per station did not result in lower completion rates for the skills-based tasks compared to the pilot OSCE.
cells.note: The comparison is between the 2024 implementation and the earlier pilot format; the study does not report a statistical test or adequate power for this outcome.

O.outcome_detail: OSCE circuit reliability measured by Cronbach’s alpha

cells.quote: With one exception, the calculated reliability (Cronbach’s alpha) of the circuits exceeded 0.80 (mean 0.84, SD 0.06). The lower coefficient in Circuit 3 (α = 0.68) reflects ceiling effects in leniently rated communication items and a narrow spread of candidate ability within this circuit rather than a deficiency of the station blueprint.
cells.note: The study reports a comparison of circuit reliability, not a manipulated instructional treatment.

O.outcome_detail: number of sites offering block-practicum qualification

cells.quote: There are programs for BP qualification at 18 sites, with required attendance at 15 of these sites. A similar number of programs exist to qualify for the practical year (n=17) and are somewhat less often mandatory (12 von 17).
cells.note: The study compares descriptive site counts with a prior 2016 survey; no significance test, equivalence test, or power analysis is reported.

result.effect: 15 of 18 sites in 2024 vs 14 of 18 sites in 2016

cells.quote: There are programs for BP qualification at 18 sites, with required attendance at 15 of these sites. At that time, 30 of 37 sites participated: 18 conducted BP qualification (obligatory at 14), 15 conducted qualification for the practical year (obligatory at 9).

cells.quote: A similar number of programs exist to qualify for the practical year (n=17) and are somewhat less often mandatory (12 von 17).
